title: Parallel-coupled band-pass filter in stripline: three half-wave resonators between 50 Ω feeds, coupled by four quarter-wave sections, planes 4 mm apart in PTFE (εr = 2.2), designed for 5 GHz, 10 % bandwidth, 0.1 dB Chebyshev ripple: its band edges and transmission against the ideal coupled-line cascade
source: Cohn's design of parallel-coupled filters (S. B. Cohn, Parallel-coupled transmission-line-resonator filters, IRE Trans. MTT 6(2):223–231, 1958; G. L. Matthaei, L. Young, E. M. T. Jones, Microwave Filters, Impedance-Matching Networks, and Coupling Structures, McGraw-Hill 1964, §§4.05, 10.02): the 0.1 dB Chebyshev prototype g = 1.0315, 1.1474, 1.0315, inverters J01 Z0 = √(πw/2g0g1), J12 Z0 = πw/(2√(g1g2)), Z0e,o = Z0[1 ± JZ0 + (JZ0)²]: 77.13/38.10 Ω and 58.26/43.82 Ω, the strips' widths and gaps from Cohn's coupled-strip mapping inverted (IRE Trans. MTT 3(5):29–38, 1955), the 50 Ω feeds' width from his stripline (IRE Trans. MTT 2(2):52–57, 1954), each section λ/4 at 5 GHz less the open end's extension Δ (the middle of its bracket, as in stripline-ends: 0.692 mm for the 2.33 mm strips, 0.723 mm for the 3.12 mm ones). The reference is the ideal TEM cascade of the open-circuited coupled sections' chain matrices (A = D = (Z0e + Z0o)/(Z0e − Z0o) cos θ, B = j[(Z0e − Z0o)² − (Z0e + Z0o)² cos²θ]/(2(Z0e − Z0o) sin θ), C = 2j sin θ/(Z0e − Z0o); E. M. T. Jones, J. T. Bolljahn, IRE Trans. MTT 4(2):75–81, 1956), θ = β(ℓ + Δ) with Z0e, Z0o of the strips as built, between 50 Ω (emcraft-theory::coupled::CoupledFilter, evaluated apart from the solver)

quantities.reason: the ideal cascade leaves out the steps in width at the resonators' middles, the open ends' fringing beside the coupled strip (Δ is a single strip's) and the box; the mesh is coarse for the end sections' 0.18 mm gaps (their odd impedance −1.3 % at this grading, the coupling a little strong, the band a little wide); −0.42 % measured, linear between points 50 MHz apart
